item.title: Buffalo Sabres Could Offer Red Wings Another Dylan Larkin Trade Path
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings have a Dylan Larkin problem, and the Buffalo Sabres might have something that could help solve it. Unfortunately for Detroit, there’s one rather significant obstacle standing in the way: Larkin himself. Buffalo has been linked to the former Red Wings captain for weeks, with NHL insider Chris Johnston reporting that the Sabres made a substantial offer for the 30-year-old center. But while Buffalo’s collection of young talent could make it an attractive trading partner, Larkin has reportedly refused to include the Sabres among his approved destinations. That leaves Detroit staring at an intriguing possibility it cannot currently pursue without the player’s cooperation. Oct 22, 2026; Vancouver, British Columbia, CAN; Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) skates against the Vancouver Canucks in the second period at Rogers Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Buffalo Sabres Reportedly Made Significant Dylan Larkin Offer According to Chris Johnston’s reporting, detailed by The Hockey Writers , Buffalo submitted what was described as a significant offer for Larkin earlier this month. The exact proposal has not been publicly confirmed, but the interest appears to be legitimate. TSN insiders Pierre LeBrun and Darren Dreger have also identified Buffalo as a team interested in acquiring the Michigan native. However, Dreger indicated that Larkin was unlikely to approve a move to the Sabres, creating a major obstacle for both organizations. That remains the central problem in Detroit’s effort to navigate Larkin’s limited trade list . A compelling offer means very little if the player refuses to authorize the move. And with Larkin carrying a full no-movement clause, the Red Wings cannot simply send him to Buffalo because they like the return. Could Buffalo’s Young Centers Interest Detroit? Here’s where things become interesting from Detroit’s perspective. The Sabres have several young centers who could potentially fit the Red Wings’ long-term plans, including Noah Ostlund, Konsta Helenius, and Jiri Kulich . All three were listed on Buffalo’s opening-season roster, although Helenius was placed on injured reserve on November 12. Ostlund might be particularly intriguing because of his offensive upside, although Buffalo’s commitment to him complicates any hypothetical deal. The 22-year-old signed an eight-year, $52.8 million extension in September, demonstrating that the Sabres view him as an important part of their future. Helenius, meanwhile, offers another potential young-center option, while Kulich has shown promise as an offensive contributor. There is no confirmed report that Buffalo has offered any of these players for Larkin, but they illustrate why the Sabres could be an interesting trading partner. item.title: ‘Give him the Heisman’: Opposing coach praises Jeremiah Smith after Ohio State loss
item.description: Oct 17, 2026; Bloomington, Indiana, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) lines up pre-snap during the first quarter against the Indiana Hoosiers at Merchants Bank Field at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Nebraska picked up the biggest win of Matt Rhule’s tenure on Saturday, beating No. 14 Ohio State 31-28 in Lincoln and likely ending the Buckeyes’ College Football Playoff hopes. But even after the win, Rhule had plenty of praise for the opponent’s biggest star. Rhule said that Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith should win the Heisman Trophy, and that he’s never competed against a player as “talented and special.” Nebraska Upsets Ohio State Nebraska jumped out to a 21-7 lead in the second quarter, but Ohio State battled back to tie the game at 21 in the third quarter. The Huskers then pulled away in the fourth quarter on a 33-yard field goal and a 26-yard touchdown pass, before holding on after a late Buckeyes touchdown. Smith did his part, finishing with 165 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including a 67-yard score on Ohio State’s first drive. But the Buckeyes managed just 76 rushing yards, while Nebraska ran for 176. The loss drops Ohio State to 7-4, and it’s the Buckeyes’ latest setback in a frustrating season. Smith drew criticism earlier this month when one longtime Ohio State reporter called him “ a petulant child ” for his frustration on the sideline during the team’s loss to Oregon. For Nebraska, which also improved to 7-4, it was the program’s first win over Ohio State since 2011. ‘Give him the Heisman’ While the Buckeyes might have lost the game, Rhule didn’t hesitate to praise Ohio State’s biggest during his on-field interview with Fox’s Jenny Taft after the game. “Jeremiah Smith, give him the Heisman. I mean, we doubled him,” Rhule said . He doubled down during his postgame press conference. “I don’t think I’ve ever competed against a player as talented and special — and I’ve had a chance to play against a lot of them — than that kid Jeremiah Smith. That man, he is unbelievable, the way he can absolutely just tilt a game,” Rhule said . Smith is widely considered the top player in college football. While Ohio State has fallen out of the College Football Playoff conversation in recent weeks, Smith has remained at or near the top of the Heisman Trophy odds. Rhule seems to think it would be well-deserved if he took home the hardware next month. item.title: Mathew Barzal’s return has been an Islanders boost — even if it involves some rare patience
item.description: Barzal DETROIT — Three games into his return from injury , Mathew Barzal is, perhaps with a veneer of caution, feeling good. His minutes, as you’d expect being on the third line, are down over four minutes per night, but he’s produced a point per night with good underlying numbers, albeit over a small sample. It is, in short, as good as the Islanders might have expected after Barzal missed the season’s first 18 games with lingering knee issues from an injury suffered two seasons ago. “Not bad,” Barzal told The Post before the Islanders faced Detroit on Saturday. “It’s gonna take a second just to get my legs and cardio back. Just timing and everything. I think I’ve been fairly solid. Feel pretty comfortable out there. Especially the Columbus game. I feel pretty similar to last year.” That is an interesting coda, as Barzal said upon his return that he felt at 80 percent for much of last season, and was managing his knee extensively in between games. Much like it has so far this year, though, that didn’t seem to impact his production, as Barzal had 72 points in 81 games and averaged the most ice time of his career. New York Islanders center Mathew Barzal (13) skates with the puck against the Columbus Blue Jackets on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, at UBS Arena in Elmont, N.Y. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While the Islanders will almost certainly look to boost Barzal’s workload at some point soon if everything keeps going well , they are in the luxurious situation of not needing to rush. Their top two lines are humming along well, and they have enough depth down the middle that the matchup advantage created by Barzal being on the third line is something coach Pete DeBoer has been happy to have in his pocket. “I think he’s getting better every night,” DeBoer said. “I like his mindset. He’s playing a mature game for us as far as with the puck and not trying to push too much, which is the natural instinct when you come back. You want to make a difference. He’s a difference-making guy. But he’s picking his spots. He’s got good patience in his game.” Patience hasn’t always been Barzal’s M.O., but — whether related to his knee or not — he does seem to be playing a more concise game. His average shift length, for example, is down by five seconds compared to last season, though that could be affected both by a small sample and by DeBoer’s bench management, which has seen drops in that statistic throughout the lineup. Perhaps the biggest difference with Barzal back in the fold is simply the added depth it gives the Islanders lineup, and the subsequent confidence that seems to give everybody. item.title: Maple Leafs Healthy Scratch Veteran In Surprising Move
item.description: Oliver Ekman Larsson Maple Leafs Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs, who have lost eight straight games, made a surprise decision for their lineup on Saturday night. The Maple Leafs take on the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday in what is a must-win game. If they are going to win, then they will need to do so without one of their veteran defenseman. Maple Leafs Scratch Oliver Ekman Larsson According to Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller, the team has decided to shake up its lineup by making veteran defenseman Oliver Ekman Larsson a healthy scratch. “Jim Hiller confirms Oliver Ekman-Larsson is a healthy scratch for Leafs tonight,” wrote TSN reporter Mark Masters on his X. Jim Hiller confirms Oliver Ekman-Larsson is a healthy scratch for Leafs tonight @TSN_Sports — Mark Masters (@markhmasters) November 21, 2026 We knew that the Maple Leafs were going to make some changes to their lineup after losing eight games in a row, but it’s still surprising to see the team give a healthy scratch designation to Ekman Larsson. Despite his struggles this season, Ekman Larsson has been a staple of the Maple Leafs’ defense since he joined the team two years ago, so this is a big surprise to see him as a healthy scratch. Maple Leafs Could Have Traded Oliver Ekman Larsson Last Year At last season’s trade deadline, former Toronto GM Brad Treliving was said to have multiple trade offers on the table for Ekman Larsson, who was having a great season for Toronto. But he decided to hold onto him instead of trading him. That looks like a big mistake in hindsight, as Ekman Larsson only has one assist in 24 games this season, compared to 8 goals and 39 points last year in 74 games. The Maple Leafs likely would have gotten a draft pick or two for him at last year’s trade deadline, but now, his trade value is gone, and the Maple Leafs may have to actually attach an asset to move his contract out following this healthy scratch. Ekman Larsson is owed $3.5 million this year, and next year, as part of his four-year, $14 million free-agent contract he signed after he left the Florida Panthers. The deal was looking good for the Maple Leafs at first, but not anymore. item.title: 49ers veteran receiver’s recent departure hints at Mike Evans’ imminent return
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers release Brandin Cooks to make room for a potential Mike Evans return. It’s unknown if Mike Evans will play in the 49ers’ highly anticipated matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, but the team’s latest move indicates a potential return. NFL insider Adam Schefter revealed on Saturday that the 49ers waived veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks, which would create a spot for Evans. Mike Evans lining up at wide receiver in an NFL game. AP Photo/Jed Jacobsohn Cooks was signed to the 49ers’ practice squad as insurance to help what was an already injury-depleted wide receiver room as the team was without Evans at the time due to a hip injury. On Oct. 1, Cooks was promoted to the team’s active roster, a few weeks before Evans went down with an Achilles injury in Week 6 against the Commanders. This past week, the 49ers have been hinting that Evans could be active for Sunday’s game as he flew to Colorado Springs, Colo. , to practice with the team as it prepared to adjust to the altitude in Estadio Azteca — sitting 7,350 feet above sea level. 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel sprinting down the sideline. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cooks, 33, primarily struggled with San Francisco this season, having only five receptions for 58 yards in five games. Before Evans was injured, he was the team’s leading receiver and was establishing a promising connection with quarterback Brock Purdy, having 27 receptions for 420 yards and three touchdowns through six games. Evans’ looming return to the 49ers’ roster this week comes a week after Deebo Samuel returned from a hamstring injury and had a two-touchdown performance in last week’s 46-40 win against the Cowboys. Deebo Samuel sprinting down the sideline. AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez It’s unknown what the future holds for Cooks. San Francisco might welcome him back to the practice squad after wide receiver Christian Kirk revealed on Wednesday that he had knee surgery on his meniscus. The team is also without De’Zhaun Stribling and third-year wide receiver Ricky Pearsall — who will be out for the rest of the season.

item.title: Miami Heat Vice City Jerseys Spark Massive Resale Frenzy After GTA 6 Launch
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat are riding a wave of pop culture hype that has nothing to do with basketball points. Fans are scrambling to grab limited edition “Vice City” jerseys tied to the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. These special uniforms have turned into instant collector’s items with prices skyrocketing on the secondary market. The team released the gear for a game earlier this week, and the demand was immediate and intense. Rockstar Games announced that the new video game sold $3.79 billion in just 24 hours. That massive launch created a fever pitch for anything branded with the Vice City name. The Heat jumped on this trend by offering the jerseys to ticket holders for one game only. Scarcity is the key driver here, as fans who missed out are now paying steep prices to own a piece of the moment. Resale Numbers Hit Stratospheric Levels The market for these jerseys moved fast and hard. Data from eBay shows that the top sale for a full bundle including the jersey and shorts reached $2,000 on release day. Three separate sales crossed the $1,000 mark within the first few days. This kind of price jump shows just how desperate some fans are to own the gear. Average prices for the jerseys alone have settled around $300. Sales range from $250 to $400 depending on the listing. In just three days, there were 285 total sales recorded on eBay for the Miami Heat Vice City set. The average sale price for those items sits at $348.57. These numbers prove that the item has value far beyond its retail cost. A New Twist on City Connect Tradition The Heat have a long history of using their alternate uniforms to honor local culture and history. They previously explored the Miami Vice theme in December 2020. This new release takes that concept further by leaning directly into the GTA 6 video game connection. The design features the VICE logo in its final format, blending the game’s aesthetic with the team’s identity. This partnership is part of a broader effort involving Fanatics and the Cactus Jack brand owned by Travis Scott. That brand has already seen success with Topps cards and exclusive releases for Wrestlemania. The collaboration brings a streetwear vibe to the court that appeals to a younger demographic. It also bridges the gap between sports fans and gaming enthusiasts in a way few teams have tried before. The Fear of Missing Out Drives Demand Many fans who want the jersey do not live in Miami or have tickets to the game. This creates a sense of fear of missing out among the wider fan base. item.title: In epic comeback, Monmouth beats Campbell 55-49 on last-second TD
item.description: Destiny defied Monmouth. The fickle mistress of the football universe plagued the Hawks with officiating errors and self-inflicted mistakes in a crucial season finale on the road against Campbell . But with 39 seconds left and Monmouth trailing 49-47, she offered a glimmer of favor. Quarterback Frankie Weaver heaved a pass that could've been intercepted, and instead the ball bounced off a Camel defender and into the hands of receiver Christian Harrison at the 19-yard line for a 50-yard gain. That break of fate was all it took for the Hawks. Because they're not a product of destiny, they're a force of their own making. And individually, there was no more palpable force than wide receiver Tra Neal. On one final contested fade route, the star redshirt junior would not be denied as he caught the game-winning 17-yard touchdown, his fourth of the day, with 20 seconds remaining to complete Monmouth's incredible 55-49 comeback win over Campbell on Saturday. "This moment—it's as good as they come," Monmouth head coach Jeff Gallo said. "Our guys fought so hard. Resilient in how they finished the game. And they fought together in the fourth quarter specifically. We've had a lot of great wins in this program, and this is just another great one." It was one final instance in a long pattern of resilience and resolve from the FCS No. 20 Hawks. The two teams were tied 28-28 at halftime, but No. 21 Campbell (8-4) surged with 14 unanswered points to take a 42-28 lead into the fourth quarter. Monmouth (9-3) could have conceded after electing to go for a two-point conversion down 42-34 and not getting it, which beget another failed attempt later that left them down 49-40 with 8:03 remaining. "It all blew up in my face. I was aggressive the entire second half. We were gonna be aggressive though. I wasn't gonna sit there and let the clock bleed out," Gallo said. "We were gonna be active participants and win this game, all the way through. Sometimes it goes your way, it didn't. From the onside kick to the blocked punt to the two-point plays. But our guys kept fighting." It seemed as though another decisive blow had beset them when the Hawks cut the lead to 49-47 with less than two minutes left and then recovered a remarkable onside kick, only for the officials to call a non-existent offsides penalty that negated a play that would've turned the tide for Monmouth. But it didn't matter, the force of the Hawks superseded that ill-timed bit of erroneous intervention. Neal produced an exceptional effort in the receiving game with nine catches for 249 yards and four touchdowns. While Weaver was fortunate on that last heave, he was in complete control aside from that play with another spectacular gun-slinging performance that was somehow even better than what he showed the previous week when he was rated as the best passer in the FCS. item.description: Credit: USA Today network via Reuters President Donald Trump has spent the last year championing Pete Rose and Roger Clemens for the Baseball Hall of Fame. But when he was asked about Barry Bonds on Saturday, his argument fell apart pretty quickly. Calling in to Fox News, Trump insisted that Bonds’ case is “different” from Clemens’, even though both players were accused of using performance-enhancing drugs. As he tried to explain the difference, Trump eventually landed on the claim that Bonds “just looked like he took drugs,” a comment which quickly sparked outrage. ‘It’s different’ Trump called in to Saturday in America , the Fox News show hosted by his former press secretary Kayleigh McEnany. McEnany, whose husband Sean Gilmartin is a former New York Mets pitcher, told Trump that her husband and her soon-to-be brother-in-law believe Bonds belongs in Cooperstown. Trump has long pushed for Rose, who was made eligible for the Hall after his death, and he issued Rose a full pardon for his 1990 tax conviction on Thursday. He has also called Clemens, a vocal supporter of his, one of the greatest pitchers ever. But Trump drew a line with Bonds, at least at first. “Well, it’s different. Pete didn’t take drugs. And Pete was Charlie Hustle,” Trump said . He then pointed out that Clemens has always denied using steroids, before seemingly realizing that Bonds has done the same. “And Roger Clemens said and stated strongly he never took drugs. Barry Bonds, I think, said that too. But a lot of— I mean, look, he was such a great player. You know, he was a great player before the so-called drug excursion, if that ever took place. But I think, and I’ll have to look at it, and I’ll consider what you’re saying too, by the way. He was— I watched him. The problem is he just looked like he took drugs. I mean, you know. Yeah, but now he’s denied it, and Roger Clemens has strongly denied it,” Trump said. Trump eventually promised McEnany that he would “take a look” at Bonds, while insisting that Clemens “should be in the Hall of Fame immediately,” he said . item.title: Dan Campbell Hints at Lions’ Defensive Shift in Week 11
item.description: Bleacher Report's Alex Kay argued the Detroit Lions should avoid a Brian Branch contract extension this offseason. Getty The Detroit Lions’ safety depth chart has gone from a thin unit to one of the deepest groups on their roster. Head coach Dan Campbell noted that right now the Lions’ plan is to rotate at least four different safeties into the mix in the Lions’ Week 11 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Campbell was asked if the team could use more of their safety depth to sub-in for their lack of linebacker depth. The Lions coach made it clear that the team has a plan. “I would say we’ve got a lot of packages, and our plan is that everybody’s got a role,” stated Campbell on Friday. “We’re trying to use everybody that we can in that defensive room. So like all those safeties, we want to use them. There’s a role for all those guys. And now you get Kerby (Joseph) back in the fold, so we’ve got a couple of things that we can do here and have flexibility to do.” The team is getting Joseph back after missing him for the past year. Brian Branch also just returned from an Achilles injury. Detroit Lions Have Safety Depth Entering Week 11 Those two had been out through the first seven games. So, the Lions have been able to find depth. Chuck Clark has been starting for Joseph all season. They also added Andre Cisco via a trade from the New York Jets. Beyond that, a rookie fifth-round pick has taken some snaps at safety. Abney might not be active, as the team has four legitimate options who can step in for the Lions in Week 11. Campbell made it clear that the team is going to use Joseph in a rotational role at first. They do not want to push him too hard. So, between rotating in Joseph, the versatility of Branch and then the sub packages that can bring in an extra safety, the team seems to have a plan. Lions Have Secondary Questions Entering Week 11 Roger McCreary typically plays in the slot for the Lions. However, he also plays on the outside when the team doesn’t need a slot option. The Lions are very thin on outside cornerback depth, so one thing they could lean on is putting McCreary on the outside and sliding Brian Branch into the slot. As noted, the team is also thin at linebacker. Putting someone like Cisco into the dime role would suffice for the linebacker depth. Between Clark and Joseph, they have two back-end threats that they could rotate as well. Then Cisco and Branch can rotate into the box role, with one of them being a slot and the other being a dime when they need an extra safety. Overall, it could lead to the four of them getting plenty of snaps. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion.
